What data the app uses, why, who sees it, and how to request corrections or deletion.

Your account name, email, and phone number; services assigned by Southbound; your responses (accept or reject, with reason), your incidents, and the location of your check-in, check-out, and incidents.
To coordinate services, verify arrival at the meeting point and punctuality, and handle incidents.

Coordination (administration) sees all of the above. The other person on your tour sees your name, phone number, and whether you accepted. Only Coordination sees your location, rejection reasons, and incidents.

While you have a service map open, GPS is read every few seconds to show your position, distance to the meeting point, and speed. That stays only on your phone and is neither stored nor sent. Only the location at the moment of check-in, check-out, or an incident is sent. Leaving the map stops GPS: we do not track you in the background or outside a service.

In Firebase (Google), whose servers may be located outside Chile, and on the project server. It is kept for the duration of the project. To display map weather, Open-Meteo is queried using only an approximate area (~1 km), not your exact position.

In Settings → Privacy you can download everything we store about you and ask for it to be deleted; Coordination reviews the request and, once approved, your data and account are deleted. You can also ask Coordination to correct your data or object to its use.
Lince Track is an academic prototype (Duoc UC, DSY1105). The services, passengers, and agencies shown are fictional.
